# Round 3: neuromuscular and metabolic candidate decisions

**Evidence cut: 4 November 2026.** This is a delta review of the prior portfolio, plus nine additional named candidate screens. Research only: no outreach, purchases, experiments or remote repository changes. The companion JSON contains the structured evidence and source registry.

## Decision

**Keep BLU3797 as the first neuromuscular proof investment and add two serious new candidates: exact 8015-P2 for MFN2-CMT2A, and human translation of Pip8b2-conjugated DNM2 exon-skipping PMO.** Both new directions have useful function after established disease in animals. Neither has established the human functional and exposure window needed for an S-tier designation.

The most useful progress on BLU is practical: there are publicly specified alternative MTM1 patient-cell starting materials and a public target-engagement construct. That reduces dependence on one supplier model or an investigator's discretionary access. It does not add a human drug-response result. Equally useful, scrutiny narrowed overly broad claims about a complete synthetic route and a readily transferable assay.

A third, lower-priority functional reserve is topical XIB4035. It comes from older post-onset work, not this year's publication cycle. Six other candidates were retained as explicit screens with hold, deprioritize or benchmark decisions. Their presence in the ledger is evidence of screening, not an attempt to fill a shortlist.

## Inventory control and counting

Alias searches across the repository snapshot and a structured search of all **622 prior coverage records plus 30 generated proposals** found no prior candidate record for any of the nine new entries below. The search included molecule codes, principal aliases, target terms where specific, and publication identifiers. The JSON records the aliases and zero-match results. New to this inventory does not mean newly invented, unpatented, available for licensing, or unstudied elsewhere.

8015-P2, parent 8015, MiM111 and Chimera C count as one mitofusin family. They remain different test articles. Murine PPMO6 and the separate patented human oligos count as one translation direction, not two independent efficacy discoveries. BLU is an update and adds nothing to the new-candidate count.

| Record | Exact decision unit | Disposition | Main decision constraint |
|---|---|---|---|
| R3-NM-01 | 8015-P2, MFN2-CMT2A | Advance staged independent human-function proof | Exact P2 has no demonstrated mature human neuromuscular rescue; same-allele/group concentration of evidence |
| R3-NM-02 | Published Pip8b2-PMO6, DNM2-CNM; separately selected human sequence | Advance bounded human translation | Human sequence, delivery and force must be established together |
| R3-NM-03 | CKD504, GARS1-CMT2D | Hold exact-asset priority | Unresolved public code-to-structure mapping; maturation/excitability confounding |
| R3-NM-04 | XIB4035 topical, established small-fiber dysfunction | Functional reserve | Exact salt/identifier consistency and human sensory function |
| R3-NM-05 | NV354, complex-I Leigh disease | Deprioritize chronic-disease pitch | Prevention-dominant evidence, no lifespan extension, exposure questions |
| R3-NM-06 | Surlorian/ARM210/S48168, RYR1 myopathy | Active clinical benchmark | Existing phase2 program; new independent value not established |
| R3-NM-07 | Ignaseclant/NMD670, CMT | Active clinical benchmark; duplicate pitch deprioritized | Primary clinical endpoint negative |
| R3-NM-08 | Decitabine, recessive RYR1 myopathy | Hold systemic repurposing | Chronic useful-function versus DNA/marrow injury window |
| R3-NM-09 | ARD-1676, SBMA | Defined-material mechanistic reserve | Target degradation/transcript rescue is short of useful function |

## 1. BLU3797: what actually changed

### A broader, defined human-model route

Coriell **GM06813** is a cataloged MTM1 fibroblast line with an exon-8 frameshift; **GM24509** is a different cataloged genotype, **c.1180G>C, p.D394H**. The Sarepta/Murdoch patent explicitly describes reprogramming these fibroblasts at iXCell and generating immature myotubes. Its cell experiments measure DNM2 suppression, not force. These sources establish starting materials and a disclosed route, not ready qualified muscle tissues or validated independent drug responders. [NM-S04–06]

This complements the previously identified Curi **p.L463S** force model. A defensible initial program can therefore specify residual-function and frameshift backgrounds without making an investigator email the scientific gate. The work still includes line authentication, mature tissue formation, stable deficit qualification and a genetic correction/restoration control. The catalog genotypes must remain attached to results; three backgrounds cannot be replaced by three clones of one line. [NM-S35]

The key proposed decision is whether the model is rescuable **after** a stable deficit. If genetic restoration cannot recover force, a negative BLU result would not cleanly falsify the target. If restoration works but engaged PIK3C2B reduction does not, the target thesis becomes substantially weaker.

### Chemistry, engagement and selectivity are more specific

The BLU article discloses the S stereoisomer, analytical characterization and key final synthetic steps from an advanced intermediate. It does not, in the material inspected, establish an independently reproduced end-to-end route. Its live-cell panel reports 68.2 nM PIK3C2B potency but omits cellular PIK3C2A and PIK3CB curves. The published engagement assay uses an in-house tracer. No unbound muscle/brain exposure or exposure-linked chronic neural margin was located. [NM-S01–02]

Addgene now publicly lists **NanoLuc-PIK3C2B vector 238834**. This supplies a defined construct, not the missing tracer or a validated transfer of the original assay. It changes the implementation problem from an unspecified proprietary assay to a tractable public-component assay-development task. [NM-S03]

The proposed first release should establish authenticated material, assay performance and a common free-concentration scale before expanding efficacy. Include the missing cellular selectivity comparisons because a single-concentration binding panel cannot establish the functional selectivity needed at sustained muscle engagement. If the assay cannot be rebuilt with an independently characterized tracer, use a validated orthogonal engagement/target-perturbation approach and explicitly avoid claiming numerical equivalence to the original NanoBRET values.

Do not use PITCOIN chemistry as though it were a matched C2β inhibitor: its relevant selectivity is centered on C2α. PI-701 also lacks the necessary established selectivity to serve as a clean orthogonal C2β control. Genetic PIK3C2B reduction is the stronger initial control. [NM-S08–09]

### Genetic neural risk is a constraint, not a deterministic prediction

The primary epilepsy study explicitly discusses incomplete penetrance, an unaffected transmitting father and a tested variant retaining kinase activity. It also supports neuronal consequences of heterozygous loss. Those observations justify a functional neural exposure comparison; they do not provide a drug concentration threshold or make seizures inevitable with reversible inhibition. [NM-S07]

**Advance exact BLU** only after reproducible post-deficit human force and fatigue benefit, engagement concordance and a usable neural/hepatic separation. **Advance the target but replace the compound** only if orthogonal inhibition works while BLU fails on its own distribution or chemistry. A peripheral successor would be a separately scored project. **Stop** if qualified, MTM1-restorable tissue repeatedly fails despite target engagement, or if useful inhibition and relevant injury cannot be separated.

This review increases operational confidence. It does not justify raising BLU's biological maturity beyond the prior bounded-proof decision.

## 2. 8015-P2: the best additional neuromuscular lead

### The exact-article chain matters

The 2020 work's four-patient neuronal experiments used **Chimera C**, whereas its animal reversal used **MiM111**. The 2024 human T105M neuronal experiments used the **8015 mixture**. Exact **8015-P2** was tested in older knock-in mice, and then in older knock-in rats in 2026. Human data from the family cannot be relabeled exact-P2 evidence. [NM-S11–12]

The rat paper reports randomization and blinded testing. Its dose cohorts contain four rats per dose and seven WT references; the highest-dose cohort stopped once values appeared normal. An acute mitochondrial-motility experiment used a substantially higher dose than the chronic functional regimen. Treat the endpoint-specific denominators and exposure differences as part of the evidence, not footnotes. [NM-S10]

There is real reason to pursue this: a repair hypothesis with established disease and organ-level function is more valuable than another image-based mitochondrial screen. There is also a concentrated failure mode: apparently broad replication may mostly represent one allele and one research network. The next experiment should deliberately reduce that concentration.

### Public material and active development

The 2024 article provides synthesis/chiral-separation information defining P2. A custom-chemistry brief must attach the correct chiral reference; generic piperine or an unspecified 8015 mixture is not acceptable. The mixture's protein-binding and brain-partition numbers cannot be assigned to P2. P2's enterohepatic behavior is a reason to measure human-relevant free exposure rather than simply celebrate a longer mouse profile. [NM-S11]

An FDA orphan listing and existing mitofusin patent families show an active external development context. The orphan listing does not identify P2 as a cleared clinical candidate, and a ceased PCT listing does not erase a granted national family member. This is compatible with independent scientific proof, but it defeats a story that the family is an unowned abandoned opportunity. [NM-S13–14]

### Deciding proof, proposed rather than already demonstrated

Fund a staged **exact-P2 human neuromuscular function** study. Establish a reproducible deficit before exposure. Use T105M plus another pathogenic MFN2 background, with genetic correction controls. Compare P2 with the parent mixture, less-active P1 and vehicle. Prioritize evoked motor-neuron-to-muscle transmission, force, fatigue and direct-muscle-stimulated force. This separates improved axonal/NMJ function from a direct muscle effect or nonspecific growth.

Track mitochondrial transport and morphology as mechanistic readouts, not the final decision. Measure free drug and compare pulse versus sustained exposure, because the family papers do not establish which profile is necessary in human tissue. Add healthy neuronal and cardiac functional measurements at the same free exposures; increased fusion by itself is not proof that mitochondrial quality control remains healthy.

A convincing result would be a material ranking change: exact P2 restores useful human function after onset, across more than one variant/background, at a coherent exposure. A T105M-restricted response would still be useful but supports a narrower development claim. Stop or redesign if only the mixture works, only morphology changes, or active exposure compromises healthy function. An independent fixed-design animal replication becomes valuable after that question is answered; repeating the original figure design first would resolve less.

## 3. DNM2 PPMO: function survives a treatment-free interval, but translation is a new product choice

The 2025 Brain study specifies a murine exon-6 PMO and Pip8b2 conjugate. Late treatment produced a specific-force increase from 11.2 to 15.6 mN/mg, assessed one month after the last dose; the late disease arms had five control and four treated animals. Fibre size did not improve. The mechanism should be described as exon skipping with reduced DNM2 protein: total transcript was not substantially reduced in vivo, so demonstrated nonsense-mediated decay is the wrong claim. [NM-S15]

This is the second new lead worth a focused translation package. Force improvement with no late fibre-size correction is particularly useful to the question of muscle quality versus simply enlarging tissue. However, the precise human oligo is a development choice, not an automatic substitution of human letters into the mouse sequence.

The separate 2025 patent discloses human-targeting sequences and immature patient-myotube knockdown. Its PPMO numbering is local to that document; a patent “PPMO6” must not be assumed to be the Brain mouse PPMO6. Neither the patent nor the mouse force result establishes human contractility rescue with a selected human article. [NM-S06]

The proposed package should first select a sequence from reproducible public disclosure, authenticate the complete conjugate and identify the actual splice product. Check for a persistent truncated protein instead of assuming that a frameshift guarantees transcript destruction. In mature DNM2-mutant human muscle, compare post-deficit force/fatigue with a non-targeting conjugate, unconjugated PMO and orthogonal DNM2 reduction at a matched degree of suppression.

The differentiation question is **muscle-selective, durable useful function at tolerable exposure**. Short mouse findings are insufficient to dismiss the earlier DYN101 clinical tolerability problem, but a different chemistry and tissue distribution may address it. That possibility is testable. Do not expand the claim to MTM1 or BIN1 disease without a separate qualified functional model. Advance only when the human article and force window are established; stop if protein reduction has no functional value or if the required suppression overlaps conjugate/off-muscle toxicity.

## 4. XIB4035: an older functional reserve worth preserving

The 2014 study contains a genuine late-start sensory experiment, not just a prevention arm. It does not establish regeneration of epidermal fibres, and benefit recurred/waned with continued treatment/withdrawal. That makes the initial proposition restoration or maintenance of impaired sensory signaling, with a separate bar for a durable regeneration claim. [NM-S19]

A catalog route exists, but the supplier's product and SDS identifiers conflict. The right response is analytical reconciliation of structure and salt form, not a conclusion that the name proves stock or that an email determines scientific promise. The report and JSON retain both source documents. [NM-S20–22]

A comparatively narrow proof would use a human sensory-neuron/skin system with an established deficit, measure stimulus-evoked signals, require a plausible endogenous ligand context, and document local exposure. RET dependence would help distinguish the claimed mechanism from generic excitability. If protective sensation is impaired or the apparent benefit is merely altered nociceptive threshold, the intended restoration product has failed even if a behavioral number moves favorably.

## 5. Why the other screens did not earn immediate investment

**CKD504:** The human GARS1 study supports an assay/mechanism lead, but neurons were treated through maturation and WT firing increased. Public primary materials did not resolve the exact code-to-structure mapping. This fails the immediate exact-article gate; a sponsor reply should not be the sole reason to rank it highly. Preserve it as a comparator and revisit only after an independent material definition and mature functional question exist. [NM-S16–18]

**NV354:** The newer complex-I paper has functional promise but is prevention-dominant and does not extend lifespan. A post-onset human energy-demand test could be valuable; the existing evidence does not support promoting it over the two stronger reversal candidates. [NM-S23]

**Surlorian:** Its six-person phase1 study includes seven dosing episodes because one participant reenrolled. An active randomized phase2 began dosing in October2026. The program is an important benchmark, not an overlooked independent asset simply because it was absent from this inventory. [NM-S24–25]

**Ignaseclant:** The sponsor's 81-person CMT trial missed its primary endpoint despite selected secondary positives. Retain that negative when evaluating new CMT functional endpoints, while keeping symptomatic transmission enhancement separate from axonal repair. [NM-S26–27]

**Decitabine:** The recessive-RYR1 mouse functional result is worth recording. The chronic-use thesis still needs a meaningful separation from the compound's marrow and DNA liabilities. Approval for oncology does not supply that separation; neither does a low nominal mouse dose. [NM-S28–30]

**ARD-1676:** Public chemistry and a catalog route are stronger than for CKD504. The SBMA work nevertheless stops at target engagement and transcriptional correction rather than useful function. This is a good example of material availability being necessary but insufficient. [NM-S31–33]

## Portfolio implication

The revised process is producing better decisions because it binds a candidate to its exact material, disease state, function and deciding proof. It also makes rejection informative. CKD504 exposes an identity problem; NV354 exposes a timing problem; ARD-1676 exposes a functional-evidence gap; the clinical benchmarks expose differentiation requirements.

The next useful milestone is not another larger list of positive mechanisms. It is an independently reproducible human-function/exposure result for BLU or P2, or successful human translation of the DNM2 conjugate. These have explicit ways to fail and produce transferable knowledge if they do. None earns S-tier by literature volume, recency, patent status or convenience of supply.

# Independent challenge: topical NDC-9009 for Darier disease

4 November 2026. Scope: challenge the proposed topical proof, not repeat the originating team’s broad screen. No outreach or experiments performed.

## Decision

**Retain a bounded NDC-9009 proof, but add a formulation/exposure gate before interpreting a topical 3D result.** The most concrete new weakness is unusually low measured aqueous solubility relative to the concentration used in the Darier experiment. A second, biologically specific risk is that an activator of residual SERCA may prevent a flare more readily than reverse a lesion in which that residual protein has already been inactivated.

## 1. The nominal 5 μM concentration is not yet a topical exposure specification

The original NDC paper’s Table 1 reports NDC-9009 molecular weight 305, **PBS pH 7.4 solubility of 0.23 μM**, and 17.1 ± 1.0% SERCA activation at 2 μM. The Darier adhesion experiment uses nominal 5 μM. Thus its nominal concentration is approximately **22-fold the measured PBS solubility**. The 2023 paper also found effects on normal neuronal spine morphology at 0.1 μM, which supplies no skin safety margin but does show that the molecule is not inactive in healthy cells. [1,2]

**Inference:** this does not invalidate the Darier experiment. Protein, cosolvent, formulation, supersaturation and membrane partitioning can make culture exposure differ substantially from PBS solubility. Nor is aqueous solubility a ceiling on achievable epidermal exposure. It means that “5 μM worked in a dish” cannot be used as the delivered topical dose, unbound concentration, or penetration target without measurement. Insoluble drug can also create misleading concentration-response curves or make apparent batch effects depend on formulation history.

The first useful development step is therefore a small formulation-to-exposure bridge: authenticate the exact article, determine what fraction is dissolved under the assay conditions, and measure exposure in viable epidermis after topical application. Vehicle controls must follow the same formulation. Surface residue or total whole-skin concentration cannot substitute for delivery to the relevant living cell layer. A topical vehicle that itself changes adhesion or irritation would confound the intended mechanism.

## 2. Prevention of junction failure is not reversal of an established lesion

The Darier paper’s functional result is a short monolayer fragmentation assay during junction assembly. Its four isolates come from three donors with two ATP2A2 variants. The same paper proposes that stress can push residual SERCA toward irreversible oxidation/inactivation and reports functional protection with **5 mM NAC**; glutathione monoethyl ester also protected junctional structure. Baseline desmoplakin localization catches up by four hours without treatment. [1]

**Inference:** a positive allosteric modulator requires sufficient activatable protein. In a mature lesion with inactivated SERCA and reorganized junctional/cytoskeletal proteins, activating the remaining pool may be inadequate even if it improves fresh junction assembly. This is a specific, testable failure mode. It does not require guessing that the target is wrong.

The proposed 3D model should establish a reproducible functional barrier/adhesion deficit **before** treatment, then distinguish reversal from spontaneous recovery and from prophylaxis. An exposure-matched preventive arm can determine whether a failed reversal experiment still supports a separate flare-prevention thesis. Those are different product claims and development paths.

## 3. Comparator implications

A topical NDC program should earn an advantage over more than vehicle. **NAC is a particularly relevant mechanistic benchmark because the same disease model shows functional protection.** Its millimolar nominal dose is not evidence of inferior topical feasibility, and NDC’s micromolar nominal dose is not by itself an advantage. Compare each at an exposure that can actually be delivered, with tolerability and formulation differences measured.

CDN1163 can serve as a same-target benchmark; the label “next generation” does not establish NDC-9009 superiority in Darier skin. A clinically relevant topical retinoid is also useful when the model captures the disease features that treatment addresses. The 2026 expert consensus describes the present treatment landscape; a short adhesion assay alone should not be used to claim clinical superiority over it. [1,3]

## 4. Healthy-skin margin must be functional

No convincing topical healthy-skin exposure margin was established in the retrieved NDC sources. This is an absence of qualification, not an observed dermatotoxicity signal. A same-donor or matched healthy-skin arm should measure intact barrier, normal differentiation and tissue integrity during repeat exposure and after withdrawal. Viability alone can miss disrupted epidermal organization. The therapeutic window must cover the exposure needed to rescue established diseased tissue; a nominal concentration ratio across unrelated assays is inadequate.

## Revised advance and stop conditions

**Advance:** a reproducible topical formulation delivers authenticated NDC-9009 into viable epidermis; measured exposure restores an established functional deficit across independent donors; benefit has a useful advantage over NAC and the selected clinical benchmark; healthy skin retains normal function; and benefit persists through a relevant washout/stress challenge.

**Stop or narrow the indication:** rescue exists only during junction assembly, requires an irritating or otherwise confounding vehicle, cannot be reproduced at measured dissolved exposure, or fails against the simpler comparator. If only prophylaxis works, retain a distinct prevention hypothesis rather than calling the result lesion repair. No owner reply is needed to make this scientific decision.

## Primary sources

1. [Harmon et al., Science Advances 2026, DOI 10.1126/sciadv.aee1599](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13440392/) — full primary text retrieved, refs ``, ``, ``, ``, ``. Do not count wells/repeats as independent patients.
2. [Rakovskaya et al., IJMS 2023, DOI 10.3390/ijms241813973](https://www.mdpi.com/1422-0067/24/18/13973) — Table 1 solubility and activation; normal-neuron results in section 2.3. Refs ``, ``, ``, ``. [PMC copy](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10530588/). The potency value is a response at one assay concentration, not an EC50.
3. [2026 expert consensus on Darier management, DOI 10.1007/s13555-026-01838-3](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s13555-026-01838-3) — original consensus document, ref ``; used for comparator context, not as evidence of NDC efficacy.

# ddiscov round 3 — organ conditioning, repair and reperfusion

Assessment: 4 November 2026. Repository baseline: `c241dc4c6cfa7cd5312a7237dda61a4d2af50c97`. This memo extends the portfolio register and round 2 blood/ex vivo review. It does not supersede other domain teams’ rankings.

## Decisions

**FXT-001/UAMC-3203 is the strongest newly identified organ candidate.** It has direct declined-human-lung evidence and a public chemical/material route. It merits a high-priority methods audit and a bounded comparison with the existing AAT lead. It is not yet an S-tier asset: exact human dose, donor-level magnitude, and full control details were not recoverable from the accessible primary text; independent post-transplant benefit is not established; a university spinout is already developing the exact lead.

**Retain AAT as a leading human-organ proof investment, but tighten its product definition.** The useful question is whether a potency-qualified, composition-matched ex vivo regimen creates persistent graft benefit. “Add AAT to perfusate” is already published, patented and adjacent to active clinical development. This round identifies a concrete formulation confound and a way to resolve it without waiting for correspondence.

**Do not promote CYM5442 merely because a new human-lung paper exists.** Its exact experiment is unusually inspectable, and its barrier result is useful, but oxygenation/compliance were not significantly better. Receptor loss creates a durability question. The defined biased agonist SAR247799 is a rational successor hypothesis, with a cheap discriminating proof before whole-organ work; its human microvascular negative result and documented sponsor discontinuation prevent promotion by narrative alone.

Ten new exact candidate records were screened, representing nine mechanistic families because CYM5442 and SAR247799 share S1PR1. “New” means absent from the reviewed repository/proposal inventory, not novel to science or patentable. The AAT update is an existing-lead refinement and is not included in the ten. No candidate is assigned S-tier in this review.

## 1. AAT: turn a promising literature result into a specific product proof

### What is actually demonstrated

The 2026 human study reports eight declined donor lung blocks, each split into a randomized treated/control pair, followed for 12 hours. AAT improved oxygenation/compliance and reduced fluid-loss/edema measures. That is eight biological blocks, not sixteen independent donors. The abstract does not provide exact dose or numerical effect sizes. The earlier eight-donor conference report is likely the same dataset; it should not be counted as replication. [A1, A2]

The public CSL patent describes a **different, five-donor pilot** using 10 mg/mL AAT versus saline. It does not establish protein/oncotic matching. One reported cytokine analysis was uncorrected for perfusate dilution. It includes future-tense clinical examples, which are not completed trials. Do not substitute this pilot’s dose for the unretrieved 2026 methods or add five and eight donors together without participant provenance. [A3]

The prior pig EVLP study used 3 mg/mL Zemaira with six animals per group; a separate recipient-IV study used five per group. Recipient treatment cannot establish the durability of an ex vivo-only product. The existence of a 2018 survival-model abstract was rechecked, but its full dataset and follow-up were not sufficiently accessible to upgrade the claim. [A4, A5, A6]

**Treatment-window classification:** these are injured-donor-organ reconditioning and peri-reperfusion protection experiments. They do not yet demonstrate durable reversal of established recipient graft failure. Even an improved endpoint relative to a deteriorating control need not mean restoration from the treated organ’s own baseline.

### New formulation finding

Zemaira’s label provides approximately 50 mg/mL A1PI after reconstitution and specifies functional elastase-neutralizing potency. Its reconstituted formulation contains mannitol 121–168 mM, phosphate 15–20 mM, sodium 73–89 mM and chloride 30–39 mM. The label directs use within three hours after reconstitution. It does not validate activity during a 12-hour warm recirculating EVLP run. [A7]

**Calculation, not a reconstruction of the published study:** achieving 10 mg/mL final AAT from a 50 mg/mL stock would make that stock 20% of final circuit volume. It would contribute approximately **24–34 mM mannitol and 3–4 mM phosphate**, before accounting for displaced perfusate. At 3 mg/mL, the corresponding fraction is 6%. Powder dissolved directly into a different fluid would create another formulation; the exact recipe matters.

This makes a saline control an incomplete causal test. Added protein, altered colloid osmotic pressure, ionic composition, mannitol and dilution can affect lung water and measured physiology. This is a plausible competing explanation, not proof the AAT result is spurious. It also creates a useful development opportunity: identify the minimum active AAT exposure that adds benefit after the physical formulation has been matched.

### Concrete product and proof route

Proposed product: a **defined, potency-qualified AAT graft-conditioning additive**, with stated starting product, reconstitution method, final perfusate composition, activity throughout circulation, recipient carryover and handling specification. A ready manufactured product is a starting route; it is not automatically an EVLP-compatible finished product.

The first stage can be resolved without scarce human lungs: compare delivered active AAT with antigen concentration, monitor circuit/tubing losses, and assess retained function across the intended warm exposure. Formulation controls should reproduce final electrolytes, osmolality, volume and measured oncotic pressure. Protein matching should use a clinically relevant albumin comparator and acknowledge albumin’s own biological effects.

The next stage should ask one causal question per independent donor pair. Separate pair blocks can compare AAT with a fully matched base perfusate and, once justified, compare it directly with FXT-001. Pairing must preserve the donor as the statistical unit; repeated biopsies and timepoints do not increase the independent sample count. Endpoints should require useful postwashout gas transfer and compliance, acceptable edema, and blinded transplantability assessment, with donor-level effect estimates and confidence intervals.

A final large-animal transplant stage should isolate **ex vivo-only** treatment and measure recipient graft function after washout. Transplant survival or sustained organ function would be materially more informative than another set of cytokines. Tissue-bound material and recipient carryover must be measured so “washout” is an observation rather than an assumption.

**Advance:** the functional advantage survives composition matching, persists after washout, and appears at a reproducible potency/exposure without a recipient liability. **Stop:** physical matching explains the effect; benefit exists only while the circuit contains drug; or markers improve without useful graft function.

### Current public development facts

The CSL organ-perfusion family remains a real public rights consideration; Google’s US application page displays pending status, not a legal clearance determination. The Canadian portal lists UHN’s randomized Zemaira lung-transplant prevention trial, protocol 23-5745, as not yet recruiting, last updated 18 July 2026. That listing does not establish an ex vivo-only regimen. A new venture needs a distinguishable product/proof advantage, not merely a new name for the known use. [A3, A8]

## 2. FXT-001/UAMC-3203: the strongest addition, with an explicit methods boundary

### Evidence and material identity

The 2026 Cell paper reports functional protection in porcine liver/lung perfusion and preservation of declined human lungs in a split-organ design. FXT-002/003 are separate optimized analogues with improved mouse PK/safety evidence; they do not inherit FXT-001’s human-organ result. The human-liver lipid-peroxidation observations are target evidence, not an interventional human liver trial. [F1]

The primary full paper is publicly deposited at Liège and Leuven, but the available 15.6 MB postprint exceeded the research tool’s size limit; the normal managed download also failed. Exact dose, human donor count, effect magnitude, vehicle matching, and any transplant/washout details therefore remain **not primary-verified** in this review. Secondary descriptions say five human pairs, but that number is not promoted into the verified evidence field. [F2, F3]

This is a bounded retrieval limitation, not evidence that the material is unavailable or that an email is needed to decide whether the lead is scientifically interesting. It prevents precise quantitative ranking against the AAT study.

FXT-001 is identified publicly as UAMC-3203. The original 2018 chemistry and the granted patent disclose compound 39 and a synthetic route. Cayman lists the **free base**, CAS 2271358-64-4, molecular weight 471.7; MCE separately lists the **hydrochloride**, CAS 2271358-65-5, molecular weight 508.12. These are not interchangeable by mass. The exact form used in the organ paper still needs reconciliation. Catalog availability is a research-material route, not a received, authenticated lot or a clinical supply chain. [F4–F7]

### Counterevidence and ownership

The earlier primary multi-organ paper gives orthogonal ferroptosis support but is not fully independent of the originating team. UAMC-3203 showed substantial tissue distribution, little brain penetration, and context dependence: it did not improve the measured injury markers in TNF or polymicrobial-sepsis models. Some renal experiments were pretreatment. This argues for a defined ischemia/reperfusion indication and measured exposure, not broad anti-inflammatory “repair.” [F8]

The granted US11339124B2 page identifies Antwerp/Ghent/VIB assignees and displays active status. The university science park describes FiriX Therapeutics as developing FXT-001 for ischemia/reperfusion injury. Thus this is an active, claimed asset with public chemistry, not an abandoned free asset. No claim-by-claim freedom-to-operate opinion is made. [F5, F9]

### Narrow investable thesis

The plausible first product is an **exact FXT-001 short-exposure graft-conditioning regimen**, starting from an authenticated chemical form, with a measured free/tissue exposure specification. The intended window is after procurement injury but before or during reperfusion. It should be called preservation/reperfusion protection unless an experiment explicitly establishes an existing deficit and then demonstrates reversal.

The decisive development contrast is not another ferroptosis marker. It is whether this small molecule delivers more useful, sustained organ function than an optimized perfusate and a credible competing repair additive such as AAT. A separate dose/exposure qualification stage should establish solubility, albumin binding, circuit loss and tissue retention before assigning scarce donor lungs.

**Advance:** after the full methods are audited, donor-level benefit is large enough to change acceptance or useful graft function; the result persists through a drug-free reperfusion challenge; and recipient exposure has an interpretable safety margin. **Stop:** only lipid markers or edema shift, control mismatch accounts for the signal, the result does not persist, or effective tissue accumulation produces a graft/recipient liability. The existing spinout is a commercial-context fact; a distinctive regimen or demonstrable superiority is required for a separate value proposition.

## 3. CYM5442 and SAR247799: use a mechanistic weakness to generate a precise successor

### The inspected human-organ experiment

The accepted CYM5442 paper is openly readable. Seven donor pairs underwent six-hour EVLP with **0.05 μM CYM5442 hydrochloride** (Tocris 3601, water vehicle), in DMEM with 5% bovine albumin. Leak/edema and pressure measurements favored treatment, but **dynamic compliance, P/F and PVR were not significantly improved**. Endothelial S1PR1 protein declined by six hours; higher exposure disrupted barrier function in cell experiments. The endothelial-cell experiments used two biological donors, with technical replicates. No washout/transplant durability was demonstrated. [C1]

This has better inspectability than many candidates but a weaker functional result than a headline suggesting human lung repair. CYM5442 is useful as a well-specified mechanistic comparator. Its potential to protect a barrier and then downregulate the same receptor makes recovery after withdrawal central to the product question. Differences between DMEM/bovine albumin and clinical perfusion media also require an exposure bridge.

### Why SAR247799 is a specific, testable successor

SAR247799 is an exact biased S1PR1 agonist, CAS 1315311-14-8, with public identity and research catalog routes. Primary experiments show an activation/desensitization separation and renal/coronary endothelial protection; these findings do not establish postinjury human lung repair. No direct SAR-versus-CYM whole-organ experiment was found. [S1–S3]

In a 54-patient randomized T2D trial, the 5-mg group had a maximum placebo-adjusted brachial FMD improvement of 1.07 percentage points (95% CI 0.13–2.01). This is a macrovascular surrogate. It does not establish superiority to sildenafil merely because one comparison reached statistical significance and another did not. The sponsor’s original report states that Sanofi terminated development and reports no interpretable microvascular laser-Doppler treatment effect. No reason for the termination is established here. [S4, S5]

Human dose-escalation work also shows that higher exposures can produce heart-rate and lymphocyte effects; biased signaling does not remove all class liabilities. The Sanofi AKI-use patent US9782411B2 displays active status. Discontinuation does not mean public-domain chemistry or available commercial rights. [S6, S7]

### New proposal and stop rule

Use a low-cost human pulmonary endothelial functional comparison to decide whether **SAR247799 preserves barrier function after an established injury and through withdrawal**, with less receptor loss than CYM5442. Compare at measured free exposure and comparable target engagement; equal nominal concentrations would not be a meaningful comparison. Include the relevant perfusate protein context and assess recovery after washout.

Only a favorable result should move SAR into paired human EVLP. The desired advantage is sustained oxygenation/compliance and fluid handling, not receptor staining alone. **Stop** if its bias fails to translate in pulmonary endothelium, if withdrawal unmasks barrier failure, or if useful exposure overlaps class effects. This is a new-to-repository successor proposal within the same S1PR1 family, not a second independent human-lung discovery.

## 4. Additional exact candidates screened

| ID | Exact candidate and evidence window | Evidence that changes the decision | Disposition and next discriminating question |
|---|---|---|---|
| R3-OR-04 | **PTL060/thrombalexin**, membrane-localizing thrombin inhibitor, graft pretreatment | Pig renal hemoreperfusion improved flow; two unused human kidneys establish feasibility, not filtration rescue. In sensitized primate transplantation, local histological benefit occurred **without a survival benefit**. [T1, T2] | Narrow reserve for thrombotic graft injury. Require postwashout filtration/function against free thrombin inhibition and an inactive anchored control. Do not market the evidence as reversal of antibody-mediated rejection. Exact current construct/lot route still needs public sequence-to-material reconciliation. |
| R3-OR-05 | **MitoQ/mitoquinone**, cold kidney preservation | Human kidney reperfusion flow improved at 50 μM; urine output did not reach significance (P=.054). Independent work found rapid mitochondrial swelling/depolarization in renal cells, including at 500 nM. These different contexts do not establish a numerical therapeutic index. [Q1, Q2] | Deprioritize until exposure/toxicity is reconciled. Require viable transport/filtration, not flow or oxygen consumption alone. An oral supplement is not a qualified organ-perfusion product. |
| R3-OR-06 | **APT102/AZD3366**, optimized soluble human CD39L3 apyrase | Fourteen dogs, seven/arm, received treatment shortly after reperfusion; pulmonary function improved over three hours. A 104-participant phase 1 study established human PK/PD, with increased capillary bleeding time at higher doses. [D1, D2] | Conditional mechanistic reserve. An ex vivo-only pulse is a new route hypothesis, not the canine regimen. Require retained organ benefit with bounded residual enzyme/antiplatelet activity after washout. |
| R3-OR-07 | **M101/HEMO2life**, defined marine extracellular hemoglobin additive | Initial human work involved 58 donor pairs with secondary functional signals; OXYOP2 was designed for 450 recipients. Manufacturer publicly announced CE marking in 2022. No definitive OXYOP2 results were verified in this pass. [H1–H3] | Existing product/comparator lane. A generic oxygen-carrier thesis would enter an occupied development space; require a specific superiority/handling opportunity. |
| R3-OR-08 | **Mirococept/APT070**, membrane-targeted complement inhibitor | Initial 10-mg clinical program did not reduce DGF. The current EMPIRIKAL-2 protocol tests substantially higher organ-directed doses following saturation work. [M1] | Active incumbent/benchmark, not a fresh unexplored asset. Its dose correction is a process lesson: normalize exposure to the organ’s target burden and retention, not simply recipient body mass. |
| R3-OR-09 | **Sodium thiosulfate**, kidney preservation additive | The investigator’s site lists the randomized STS-Transplant study as actively recruiting, with one-year follow-up. The newly retrieved pig work is an abstract-level ex vivo study, not survival evidence. [N1, N2] | Monitor/benchmark. A defined accessible chemical does not itself create differentiation from an active trial of the exact use. |
| R3-OR-10 | **Inhaled sphingosine**, local donor-lung decontamination | The 2026 pig study used five lungs/group and found acute bacterial-burden reduction without measured short-term functional worsening. Four human recipient explants provided tissue-delivery observations; only one was colonized, and they were ventilated without perfusion. [P1] | Reserve only. Require incremental viable clearance over appropriate antibiotic treatment and preserved graft function in clinically representative colonized donor tissue; tissue delivery is not replicated human antibacterial efficacy. |

These candidates span ferroptosis, S1PR1 signaling, local coagulation, mitochondrial redox biology, purinergic metabolism, oxygen delivery, complement, sulfur metabolism and direct antimicrobial lipid effects. They are not ten renamings of one target.

## 5. What this changes in the search process

**Use a claim-level progression rather than a paper-level score.** A new paper can supply one part of the case—identity, target engagement, organ physiology or tolerability—without supplying all four. The strongest new example is FXT-001: the material route can be resolved publicly while exact human magnitude remains unverified. The strongest cautionary example is SAR247799: a positive publication sits beside a negative secondary endpoint and an explicit sponsor termination report.

**Make the comparator carry the rival explanation.** In AAT, the rival explanation is physical perfusate composition. In CYM5442, it is transient receptor activation with later desensitization. In MitoQ, an apparent flow advantage may coexist with mitochondrial injury. In PTL060, thrombus histology can improve without survival. These are targeted reasons to stage an experiment, not generic requests for more research.

**Separate preservation from repair in the register.** Treatment before ischemia is prevention. Treatment after procurement injury but before reperfusion can be useful conditioning without proving reversal of established organ dysfunction. A treatment must start after a documented functional deficit and restore that deficit before the stronger repair claim is earned. Postwashout and post-transplant outcomes further test whether the effect is durable.

**Do not count publicly listed material, exact authenticated material, institutional model access, and rights as one availability field.** A supplier listing can remove an entity-definition bottleneck. It cannot demonstrate a matching salt form, reproducible potency, legitimate clinical manufacture, or actual organ access. None of these distinctions requires an owner email as a scientific-selection gate.

### Recommended allocation of the next proof effort

1. Complete the public methods extraction for **FXT-001** and reconcile free-base/HCl identity; its human organ claim warrants this focused effort.
2. Prepare the **AAT matched-formulation/potency experiment**, which addresses a specific alternative explanation and produces a useful product specification.
3. Run the **SAR-versus-CYM pulmonary barrier/washout decision** before committing whole organs to a successor hypothesis.
4. Keep **PTL060 and APT102** as narrower functional reserves; hold MitoQ behind a targeted toxicity/exposure question; use M101, mirococept and STS as occupied comparator/development lanes.

The fundable unit here is a bounded proof that can remove a decisive uncertainty and change selection. It is not yet a claim that one of these molecules is obviously financeable as an independent company. Scientific selection can continue now from public evidence; commercial exclusivity remains a separate, explicitly unresolved assessment.

## Sources and retrieval provenance

URLs below are primary papers, author repositories, manufacturer documents, registry/investigator records or public patent documents. Patent-aggregator status is not a legal opinion. Sources sharing an underlying study are counted once. Search reference IDs are retained for the integrating agent, which should reopen relevant pages before user-facing citation.

Alias searches covered the repository snapshot, `portfolio_inventory.json`, and `round2_generated_concepts.json`: FXT/UAMC; M101/HEMO2life/Hemarina; PTL060/thrombalexin; mirococept/APT070; CYM5442; apyrase/APT102/AZD3366; MitoQ/mitoquinone; sodium thiosulfate; SAR247799; and sphingosine. novelty_basis.note: New to this portfolio is not patent novelty or absence of an existing commercial program.

evidence: The mouse mechanical-injury study dosed on days 7–14 and observed sensation to day 30, 16 days after dosing ended. A separate days 5–10 protocol measured day-14 function in mechanical and chemical models; this is four days off treatment, not verified pharmacokinetic washout.
Supplemental S2: day-14 surgical-model medians 4.5 at either dose versus 2.79 vehicle, total N=22 across three arms; chemical-model medians 4.585/4.625 versus 2.040 vehicle, total N=12.

Randomization and blinded secondary imaging review were reported. Primary quantifier and sensory-assessor blinding remain unresolved. Both surgical-model eyes were analyzed as independent; chemical-model injury involved one eye per mouse. Main day-30 tests against healthy controls establish neither equivalence nor a reported direct drug–vehicle contrast.

At day 30, axonal-network medians were 357.7 with vehicle and 362.1 with RM4404 (healthy 394.6). Different significance results against healthy controls do not establish a drug–vehicle structural advantage.
new_candidate_screens.independent_biological_unit: Animal is the biological block. Surgical-model eyes and repeat thresholds are nested; N=22 must not be described as 22 independent mice. Chemical-model N=12 is total across three arms, not 12 treated animals.
limitations: No retrieved independent-laboratory replication, active repair comparator, human tissue efficacy or unbound corneal exposure.
Primary-quantifier and sensory-assessor blinding remain unresolved; section 2.9 does describe blinded secondary reexamination of imaging. The supplemental questionnaire was not recovered.
Stock arithmetic implies 0.2% versus 2% DMSO. The vehicle is called similarly prepared without explicit accounting: qualification ambiguity, not proven confounding.
Stored-particle TEM does not establish chemical potency, release, sterility or shelf life.

new_candidate_screens.name: Alvelestat for pancreas preservation before islet isolation
new_candidate_screens.novelty_basis: No alvelestat/AZD9668 occurrence in the original inventory, round2 generated proposals, or round3 candidate records. Published use is not claimed to be new to science.
new_candidate_screens.exact_entity: Alvelestat (AZD9668/MPH-966), research material from AdooQ in the source study, as an additive to extracellular-type trehalose-Kyoto pancreas-preservation solution.
new_candidate_screens.functional_evidence: A 2022 primary study compared 10 porcine pancreatic isolations per group. Treated pancreata yielded more islets and higher glucose-stimulated insulin function. At a marginal transplanted islet quantity, 11/20 recipient mice reached the study's glycemic criterion versus1/20 controls; each group of20 mice came from10 isolations, two recipients per isolation.
new_candidate_screens.biological_unit: Ten pancreatic donor/isolation units per group; recipient outcomes are nested two per isolation. Twenty recipients are not20 independent drug-treated donor pancreata.
new_candidate_screens.treatment_timing: Preservation of an already procured organ before a prolonged cold-storage/isolation challenge. This is prevention of additional processing injury, not reversal of established diabetes in the donor or regeneration of lost human islets.
new_candidate_screens.comparator: Same preservation workflow without alvelestat. The paper discusses sivelestat and ulinastatin but does not establish head-to-head superiority over an optimized active preservation regimen.
new_candidate_screens.research_material_route: Defined small molecule and named research supplier in the primary methods. No current stock, received lot, salt/formulation equivalence, GMP supply or residual clearance qualification established in this review.
new_candidate_screens.model_route: Porcine pancreas isolation route is described. Human donor-isolation access has not been secured or independently reproduced here.
new_candidate_screens.exposure_product_gap: Need measured residual drug and NE activity through storage, washout and isolation; preserve digestion performance and viable functional yield at scale.
new_candidate_screens.public_commercial_facts: Mereo and Sentynl announced an option/license agreement for alvelestat in AATD lung disease on11August2026, with Phase3 initiation projected for early2027 conditional on option exercise. That is an active external program, not an islet-use license or approval. NIH lists one related graft-rejection application as abandoned; this does not establish global clearance.
new_candidate_screens.decision: Reserve for an independently differentiated islet-manufacturing proof; does not displace the leading programs.
new_candidate_screens.deciding_proof: Test donor-level functional islet yield and sustained glucose-responsive output against optimized preservation plus an active NE-inhibitor comparator, with blinded allocation, explicit recipient clustering and residual-product clearance.
new_candidate_screens.advance_condition: A reproducible human-relevant increase in usable functional islets, or reduced donor/isolation burden, that remains after washout and exceeds the strongest practical comparator.
new_candidate_screens.stop_condition: Higher counts without useful secretion or graft function, no advantage over an existing preservation additive, or residual and processing burdens that erase the gain.

existing_candidate_updates.verdict: Retain conditional proof priority; no promotion
evidence_deltas: Both culture variants lie in the SERCA2 actuator domain. Mean protein abundance is about 70% of control; it is not a measured 50%-protein-null model. Calcium imaging in the retrieved section used DD2.
DD5–7 were biopsy immunohistochemistry samples, not additional NDC-treated culture donors.
DD3–4 required Y27632 during maintenance; all DD cultures and CTL1–2 received it for consistency. It was removed 24–36 h before assays, so there is no demonstrated concurrent ROCK-inhibitor confound.

The 2023 healthy-neuron result involved spine-neck morphology at 0.1 µM, with at least 10 neurons / 70 spines from one culture batch. It is not observed skin toxicity; the 2025 intraperitoneal CNS study does not qualify topical exposure.
The Darier paper section titled Solubility assay measures protein detergent solubility, not dissolved NDC-9009.
existing_candidate_updates.decision_implication: Qualify models by measured residual SERCA function and an established, rescuable adhesion/barrier deficit. Total protein and ATP2A2 diagnosis alone do not establish suitability. Link drug exposure to ER refilling and tissue function; keep genotype and donor strata separate.

existing_candidate_updates.stop_or_narrow_if: Only junction assembly improves, benefit depends on a stressor/vehicle, no useful comparator margin exists, or the disease state lacks activatable residual protein.

existing_candidate_updates.name: AAT in donor-lung EVLP
existing_candidate_updates.exact_article: Potency-qualified plasma-derived AAT product in a defined warm-EVLP perfusate; recombinant AAT cold-storage study is supporting mechanism, not identical finished product.

independent_unit.unit: independent transplanted mouse graft/recipient; separate paired human donor blocks
independent_unit.count_boundary: New mouse arm-level sample sizes were not recovered reliably. Neither lung sides nor tissue fields are additional donors.

evidence: Independent 2018 study compared active recombinant AAT with a non-inhibitory reactive-center mutant and albumin during cold preservation. PR3/NE-null recipients were also protected; this strengthens protease-specific causality.
The inspected cold-storage regimen used 1 mg/mL AAT, 18h storage and 4h recipient reperfusion. This is separate from the warm human EVLP experiment.
limitations: Exact 2026 human AAT dose/formulation remains unverified; do not import the mouse dose.
Short post-transplant mouse protection is not long-term recipient outcome or proof of complete drug removal.
Label NE potency alone does not establish PR3 neutralization or activity after warm-circuit exposure.
existing_candidate_updates.verdict: RETAIN_CORE_PRIORITY; mechanistic confidence increases; human formulation and durable-graft gates remain.
existing_candidate_updates.decisive_next_proof: Qualify NE and PR3 inhibition in the actual warm perfusate, then compare AAT with physically matched protein/excipient control and an NE-selective comparator. Require postwashout function under recipient-like reperfusion.
existing_candidate_updates.go_rule: AAT supplies persistent useful gas-transfer/compliance benefit at qualified activity and adds value beyond the simpler comparator.
existing_candidate_updates.stop_rule: Stop the differentiated AAT product thesis if physical matching or the simpler comparator explains the useful effect, or if activity is lost before the intended treatment window.
existing_candidate_updates.material_route: Existing manufactured AAT is a public supply route. No lot, stock, warm-circuit compatibility or clinical product identity has been established here.

existing_candidate_updates.rights_and_program: Previously identified CSL/UHN context persists. The independent mechanism does not establish new commercial rights.

existing_candidate_updates.exact_article: Exact UAMC-3203 chemical form and active-moiety concentration must be fixed; free base and hydrochloride are distinct material records.

independent_unit.unit: organ donor in Cell study; individual animal in independent counter-context studies

evidence: Newly located author dataset is DOI10.17632/n7jbyznw8g.1 and describes NMR/MS data. Its metadata was inspected; spectra/files and donor-level physiology were not.

limitations: APAP and repeated systemic post-stroke exposure do not demonstrate toxicity or failure of brief ex vivo lung dosing. They limit broad mechanism/safety claims.

FXT-002/003 PK/safety findings cannot be assigned to FXT-001.

existing_candidate_updates.stop_rule: Stop a duplicate business thesis or broad repair claim if it only repeats the existing preservation result, or if functional benefit vanishes after withdrawal.

existing_candidate_updates.model_readiness: Published organ setting exists; a qualified local circuit, donor supply and exact protocol remain to be established.
existing_candidate_updates.rights_and_program: Current science-park listing still identifies FiriX as developer of FXT-001; no abandoned-asset inference.

Newly inspected source workbook verifies strong dose-dependent, ceiling-limited wire-hang observations but exposes an unresolved P22 schedule mismatch in the small late-start comparison, incomplete baseline records, and unlinked panel denominators.
existing_candidate_updates.decision: Retain leading staged human-function proof; improve route-definition confidence and narrow late-treatment evidence interpretation. No S-tier promotion.

independent_challenges.candidate_name: RM4404/WAY-262611 for delayed corneal nerve repair
independent_challenges.conclusion: Useful delayed functional signal merits independent replication. Randomization is reported. The mechanical-injury analysis treats two eyes of a mouse as independent, and its late durability comparisons are often against uninjured animals rather than direct drug-versus-vehicle tests. Supplement S2 supplies explicit drug-versus-vehicle tests, including a one-injured-eye chemical model. Do not claim equivalence to normal or count N22 eye observations as22 mice.
independent_challenges.product_note: Methods describe drug dilution from DMSO stocks into micelles; the high and low drug concentrations imply different DMSO fractions. Drug-free vehicle is described as similarly prepared, but explicit dose-matched solvent composition is not resolved. Treat this as a formulation-control qualification item, not a proven explanation of efficacy.
independent_challenges.deciding_proof: Independent, masked animal-level delayed-treatment replication with characterized formulation and matched vehicle, meaningful active comparator, post-withdrawal sensation, corneal optics and epithelial safety.
independent_challenges.additional_independent_review: A second workstream independently checked the primary paper. Section 2.9 reports blinded secondary imaging review; primary-quantifier and sensory-assessor blinding remain unresolved. At day30 axonal medians357.7 vehicle versus362.1 RM4404 do not demonstrate structural superiority from separate healthy-reference tests. Four days off treatment in the short regimen is not pharmacokinetic washout; do not merge it with the longer mechanical-injury cohort.

alias_search_basis.scope: Cumulative schema3 register including622 coverage rows,30 round2 proposals,36 round3 screens and embedded review texts
alias_search_basis.caveat: Absence under named aliases is inventory novelty only, not invention/patent novelty.

new_candidates.exact_entity: CLP290 carbamate prodrug of CLP257; Tocris 6758; CAS 1181083-81-7. Do not substitute the active parent or OV350.
new_candidates.indication: Chronic SCI spasticity with residual motor capacity
new_candidates.decision: functional_reserve
new_candidates.functional_evidence: 2018 staggered-lesion motor benefit and independent 2025 chronic complete-SCI assisted-stepping/reflex effect. Different tasks and models; not replicated unassisted walking.
new_candidates.independent_biological_units: 2018: starts 10 mice per group, ends with 8 vehicle and 10 drug at week 9. 2025: starts with 7 female rats; many endpoint analyses include 6. Paired limbs and EMG channels are nested within animals.

readiness.sourcing: public research catalog; stock/lot not verified
readiness.model: public chronicSCI assay descriptions; no execution here
readiness.exposure: 2025: single 100 mg/kg i.p. exposure; no human therapeutic exposure bridge established.
readiness.rights: issued neonatal-combination method patent exists; SCI claim mapping incomplete
readiness.differentiation: must outperform meaningful motor tradeoff of antispastic comparator; mechanism disputed

new_candidates.proposed_decisive_proof: Independent blinded vehicle/active-comparator experiment with post-deficit useful motor task, matched free exposure, force preservation and KCC2 versus GABA-A mechanism separation.
new_candidates.kill_or_narrow: Stop promotion if benefit only reflects nonspecific sedation, no force preservation, or infeasible exposure; retain target separately if exact compound mechanism fails.

Treadmill uses manual support and perineal stimulation.
CLP257 primary mechanism challenge includes GABA-A potentiation; genetic KCC2 efficacy does not prove drug specificity.
Washout behavior differs by study/endpoint; do not claim universal persistent restoration.

new_candidate_screens.candidate: RM4404/WAY-262611 for delayed corneal sensory repair
new_candidate_screens.exact_article: WAY-262611 (CAS 1123231-07-1) in the disclosed Kolliphor HS-15 micellar preparation RM4404; not a new chemical entity.
new_candidate_screens.disease_or_use: Persistent corneal hypoesthesia after stromal nerve injury.

novelty_basis.note: New to this portfolio is not patent novelty or absence of an existing commercial program.

evidence: The mouse mechanical-injury study dosed on days 7–14 and observed sensation to day 30, 16 days after dosing ended. A separate days 5–10 protocol measured day-14 function in mechanical and chemical models; this is four days off treatment, not verified pharmacokinetic washout.
Supplemental S2: day-14 surgical-model medians 4.5 at either dose versus 2.79 vehicle, total N=22 across three arms; chemical-model medians 4.585/4.625 versus 2.040 vehicle, total N=12.

Randomization and blinded secondary imaging review were reported. Primary quantifier and sensory-assessor blinding remain unresolved. Both surgical-model eyes were analyzed as independent; chemical-model injury involved one eye per mouse. Main day-30 tests against healthy controls establish neither equivalence nor a reported direct drug–vehicle contrast.

At day 30, axonal-network medians were 357.7 with vehicle and 362.1 with RM4404 (healthy 394.6). Different significance results against healthy controls do not establish a drug–vehicle structural advantage.
new_candidate_screens.independent_biological_unit: Animal is the biological block. Surgical-model eyes and repeat thresholds are nested; N=22 must not be described as 22 independent mice. Chemical-model N=12 is total across three arms, not 12 treated animals.
limitations: No retrieved independent-laboratory replication, active repair comparator, human tissue efficacy or unbound corneal exposure.
Primary-quantifier and sensory-assessor blinding remain unresolved; section 2.9 does describe blinded secondary reexamination of imaging. The supplemental questionnaire was not recovered.
Stock arithmetic implies 0.2% versus 2% DMSO. The vehicle is called similarly prepared without explicit accounting: qualification ambiguity, not proven confounding.
Stored-particle TEM does not establish chemical potency, release, sterility or shelf life.

existing_candidate_updates.verdict: Retain conditional proof priority; no promotion
evidence_deltas: Both culture variants lie in the SERCA2 actuator domain. Mean protein abundance is about 70% of control; it is not a measured 50%-protein-null model. Calcium imaging in the retrieved section used DD2.
DD5–7 were biopsy immunohistochemistry samples, not additional NDC-treated culture donors.
DD3–4 required Y27632 during maintenance; all DD cultures and CTL1–2 received it for consistency. It was removed 24–36 h before assays, so there is no demonstrated concurrent ROCK-inhibitor confound.

The 2023 healthy-neuron result involved spine-neck morphology at 0.1 µM, with at least 10 neurons / 70 spines from one culture batch. It is not observed skin toxicity; the 2025 intraperitoneal CNS study does not qualify topical exposure.
The Darier paper section titled Solubility assay measures protein detergent solubility, not dissolved NDC-9009.
existing_candidate_updates.decision_implication: Qualify models by measured residual SERCA function and an established, rescuable adhesion/barrier deficit. Total protein and ATP2A2 diagnosis alone do not establish suitability. Link drug exposure to ER refilling and tissue function; keep genotype and donor strata separate.
existing_candidate_updates.advance_if: Delayed mature-epidermis cohesion/barrier benefit exceeds appropriate NAC, CDN1163 and clinical-route comparators at measured exposure while preserving healthy epidermis.
existing_candidate_updates.stop_or_narrow_if: Only junction assembly improves, benefit depends on a stressor/vehicle, no useful comparator margin exists, or the disease state lacks activatable residual protein.

existing_candidate_updates.verdict: Strengthen comparator rationale; actual trial outcomes remain unknown
evidence_deltas: The October 8, 2026 primary abstract reports mitochondrial calcium/respiration and adhesion improvement partly via MCU; full dose and donor denominators were not recovered.
Listing ATP2A2-knockout models does not establish which model showed the adhesion result; no knockout-specific rescue is inferred.

Official registry confirms trial completion in September 2025. A mirror lists SUM-151495 version 2, dated September 8 and submitted September 10, 2026. Actual efficacy, adverse events and actual enrollment remain unread; planned 20 is not actual N.
existing_candidate_updates.decision_implication: Dantrolene provides an alternative calcium/mitochondrial comparator. Oral trial completion establishes neither topical efficacy nor failure. Investigator outreach is not a scientific-selection gate.
existing_candidate_updates.advance_if: Retrieved primary trial results or independent delayed epidermal repair establishes a route-specific advantage at feasible exposure.
existing_candidate_updates.stop_or_narrow_if: No mature functional benefit at a tolerable local exposure or worse healthy-tissue function than simpler comparators.

local_repair.s_tier_assessment: No candidate establishes an independently replicated, exposure-qualified, differentiated and transferable development case. RM4404 and APR-246 provide concrete new proof opportunities, not funding guarantees.

comparative_priority_note.APR246_vs_NDC9009: APR-246 has stronger human species/timing evidence and a more concrete published formulation. Reserve status reflects unresolved durable functional barrier/cornification, withdrawal and chronic local exposure-to-harm window, not lack of an owner response or inherently weaker efficacy. NDC also lacks mature-lesion rescue and a topical margin; the public record does not establish overall superiority. Small independent qualification of both is justified. Promote APR-246 ahead if durable barrier and a useful margin are established or NDC remains prevention-only.
comparative_priority_note.rights: Map actual claims in parallel; neither patent titles nor unanswered commercial questions decide the biology.

organ_blood.novelty_rule: New means no matching exact candidate/use found in the reviewed repository snapshot, round2 proposal inventory or round3 records; not novelty to science or patentability.

deduplication.boundary: Genistein and luteolin are distinct exact screens in the same flavonoid/cystinosis family. Generic autophagy or anti-inflammatory mentions do not establish an exact matched article/use.
